speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Dev, thanks for joining. I hear a little one in the background?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, sorry, that's Leo. He's ten weeks. Mira's got him but he might join us.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, no problem at all. Congratulations! So this is just about your grocery orders.

speaker: interviewee
text: Thanks. Sure, go for it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: So it's me, Mira, and now Leo. Before, we'd do one big shop together on a Sunday. When we brought him home from the hospital neither of us was leaving the flat, we were basically zombies for a couple of weeks, so that's when the app came out. These days Mira takes him out in the pram to the shops in the afternoon, it gets her out of the house, so we just do that.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Walk me through your last Shmuber Eats order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: It was at like three in the morning, during a feed. I just put in everything we could think of. Nappies, wipes, oat milk, bread, those frozen meals, a lot of chocolate. I hit order and went to sleep, or tried to.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. And when it came?

speaker: interviewee
text: I put it away with one hand. The other one was holding a bottle.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe four orders in total. Not lately.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: They swapped the nappies for a different size once. One size up. That was actually a problem, they leaked.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did you get a heads-up before the bags came?

speaker: interviewee
text: There was a notification, but come on, I was asleep or feeding. I saw it the next day.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: A note on Mira's phone. I add things to it, and she says I add the wrong things.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Do you both add to it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, both of us. Mostly her. I add snacks.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: Whatever was earliest. We were home all the time, so the window didn't matter at all.

speaker: interviewer
text: And now that Mira's out more, would the window be harder?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe. Two hours is a long time to stay in with a baby who wants to go out. But we don't order now, so.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Honestly, no, I wouldn't use it enough. Maybe five, if it covered everything.

speaker: interviewer
text: What if it was 9.99?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, not for how often we order. That's a lot of nappies.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. And how did you first hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: A friend had a code. Everyone on the parents' group chat has a code for something.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Would you recommend it to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, I'd tell other parents about it, sure.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What did you like most?

speaker: interviewee
text: Three a.m. ordering. Nothing else is open at three a.m.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The nappies thing. And the app sometimes forgot what I'd put in the basket if I closed it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted. Great. Did you leave a rating after any of the orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: I think I gave five stars once. I don't remember.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Have you tried the recipes section?

speaker: interviewee
text: No. I don't think we've cooked a recipe since he was born.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I don't think so. Sorry, he's starting.

speaker: interviewer
text: No problem at all. Thank you so much Dev, and good luck with Leo.

speaker: interviewee
text: Thanks, bye.
